These representative measurements describe GACT website workflows and simulated workloads. They were recorded on an Intel Core i7-1365U workstation with approximately 16 GiB RAM and R 4.4.1 on Windows. Exact software versions vary between runs; historical evidence is labeled separately. Timings do not measure the original UK Biobank manuscript analyses or establish a systematic scaling study.

## Database and CAD T2D workflows

| Operation | Threads | Wall time | Resident memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Database download and setup | 1 requested | 544.20 s | 2.68 GiB |
| VEGAS complete initial analysis | 4 decoding; serial spectra | 899.94 s | 5.88 GiB |
| LDSC | No fitter thread argument | 9.28 s | 3.02 GiB |
| GNOVA | No fitter thread argument | 6.39 s | 3.09 GiB |
| SumHer equal-marker baseline | No fitter thread argument | 12.87 s | 3.53 GiB |
| Chromosome-set LDSC preparation and fit | No fitter thread argument | 29.91 s | 3.27 GiB |
| HESS regional preparation | 4 | 1128.67 s | 3.18 GiB |
| HESS raw pair refit | No fitter thread argument | 3.61 s | 0.41 GiB |
| HESS partial pair refit | No fitter thread argument | 3.31 s | 0.43 GiB |

Database setup transfers 2.57 GiB and installs a 3.04 GiB basic database; its 544.20-second clock is a published earlier-version download/setup measurement, separate from package installation. Network conditions affect this measurement.

VEGAS covers 17,862 genes, two traits and a 503-person EUR reference. The 899.94-second complete initial analysis includes regional spectra, prepared-object conversion and alignment; input-file loading is separate. Its 5.88 GiB is the complete-worker peak including loading. Preparation uses four decoding threads while regional products/eigensolvers are serial. Component clocks are 643.36 s for spectra, 79.52 s for conversion and 97.69 s for the initial fit. A separate prepared refit takes 71.44 s, excluding the 17.26-second object-loading cost. Do not add this alternative refit to the initial workflow.

Correlation fits use 7,221,923 common marker rows. Their memory is a sampled analysis peak with inputs loaded before the clock, rather than a whole-process high-water mark. HESS prepares 1,702 regions and 18,696 components; refits reuse compact moments. SumHer is an equal-marker baseline, not an upstream LDAK comparison. Scores are reused; estimator-specific assumptions remain in the [correlation tutorial](Genetic_correlation_CAD_T2D_gcorr.html).

## Simulated association and fine mapping

The panel contains 5,000 people and 37,991 filtered markers. Downloading, simulation, QC, startup and whole-genome sparse-LD preparation are excluded from these fit times.

| Operation | Threads | Wall time | Process peak memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linear regression | 4 | 1.64 s | 153 MiB |
| Gaussian LOCO | 4 | 57.00 s | 386 MiB |
| Prior-selected LOCO | 4 | 124.12 s | 392 MiB |
| Four regional BayesC fits and posterior sets | 1 | 5.48 s (5.22–6.28) | 0.56 GiB |
| Genome-wide BayesC fit from prepared LD | 1 | 2.36 s (2.03–2.38) | 0.81 GiB |
| Genome-wide credible-set grouping | 1 | 3.95 s (3.83–4.16) | 0.52 GiB |

Association rows are single runs. Fine-mapping rows are medians of three serial repeats; memory is the median whole-process peak working set. Regional BayesC uses one chain, 1,000 post-burn sweeps and 100 burn-in sweeps over four regions containing 850, 785, 1,091 and 1,399 markers. The genome fit uses one chain and 100 sweeps without burn-in. The tutorial's two-chain calls have not been timed. These short runs measure computation, not convergence or calibrated inference.

## Existing simulated scoring evidence

The following historical standalone measurements separate score application from fitting. They are suitable as labeled representative workload evidence. They do not establish the cost of every current software version.

| Operation | Simulated workload | Threads requested | Wall time | Process peak memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total score | Artificial-LD panel; 2,000 recipients; 50,000 SNPs | 1 | 8.03 s | 192.3 MiB |
| Three synthetic pathway scores | Artificial-LD panel; 2,000 recipients; 50,000 SNPs | 1 | 6.30 s | 192.8 MiB |
| Total score | Artificial-LD panel; 2,000 recipients; 50,000 SNPs | 4 | 3.23 s | 192.9 MiB |
| Three synthetic pathway scores | Artificial-LD panel; 2,000 recipients; 50,000 SNPs | 4 | 2.66 s | 192.7 MiB |
| Total score | 1000G-derived gsim panel; 2,000 recipients; 5,360 SNPs | 1 | 1.03 s | 157.2 MiB |
| Three synthetic pathway scores | 1000G-derived gsim panel; 2,000 recipients; 5,360 SNPs | 1 | 2.41 s | 157.8 MiB |

The artificial-LD panel uses binomial/block-copy genotypes and gsim phenotypes. The 1000G-derived panel uses gsim reference-conditioned simulation from 503 EUR donors on chr22; filtering retains 5,360 SNPs. Both have 2,000 held-out score recipients and three synthetic pathway memberships. The reference-derived scores use fixed simulated effect weights, not posterior weights from a model fit. No UK Biobank data are used for these scoring measurements.

Operation clocks exclude recipient preparation, input loading and serialization; the memory peaks cover the complete R process including loading and saving. Thread counts are requested limits; runtime worker counts were not observed. Each setting is one execution. The reference-derived workload superseded artificial LD for the real-LD benchmark objective; the historical artificial-LD thread comparison remains useful with this qualification.

A different 50,000-marker workload scored a total plus 20 artificial gene-marker sets in 14.88 s at one thread and 5.31 s at four threads. Its driver did not record peak memory; memory from the rows above cannot be assigned to that combined workload.

## Historical gene set and PoPS evidence

These earlier runs do not match all current website model interfaces and settings. PoPS produces gene rankings, not individual polygenic scores.

| Operation | Threads requested | Wall time | Process peak memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Joint two-trait, three-set simulated model | 1 | 0.10 s | 102.9 MiB |
| Joint CAD/T2D gene-set model, KEGG | 4 | 3.11 s | 2997.7 MiB |
| qgg full-data PoPS ridge | 1 | 2.04 s | 410.5 MiB |
| qgg full-data PoPS BayesC | 1 | 3.21 s | 498.5 MiB |
| qgg full-data PoPS BayesR | 1 | 7.71 s | 498.3 MiB |

The simulated joint model uses four chains, 200 burn-in and 800 sampling sweeps, independent gene covariance and fixed trait/effect covariance and inclusion-pattern settings. It is not an equivalence claim for qgg BLR-MAGMA. The CAD/T2D joint timing is an earlier standalone KEGG counterpart, not the manuscript Reactome fit. Historical qgg PoPS fits the full dataset; the updated [PoPS tutorial](Gene_ranking_bayesian_pops.html) excludes the predicted chromosome from training and specifies two chains for its Bayesian calls.

## Remaining measurement gaps

| Item | What remains |
| --- | --- |
| Current Bayesian gene-set calls | No verified record matching the exact current website implementation and controls |
| Current chromosome-held-out Bayesian PoPS | No tutorial-scale timing/memory record for the updated held-out workflow; test durations are not benchmark timings |
| Memory for combined total plus 20-set run | No captured memory for this specific run; use the separately measured scoring workloads instead |
| Systematic scoring scalability | No controlled grid of recipient count, markers, set count and overlap; existing runs remain representative examples |
| Chromosome-component glma examples | Component-example time and memory |
| Two-chain fine-mapping calls | Matching two-chain measurements; retain one-chain qualification if using existing results |
| VEGAS component memory | Separate preparation/fit peaks; not required for whole-workflow reporting |

Scoring time, memory and separate total/pathway costs are already available for the workloads above. More measurements would be needed for a controlled scaling grid, not to fill a general absence of scoring evidence. Final output-size reporting can use saved artifact inventories with consistent definitions.

## Evidence and reproducibility

The [consolidated evidence table](../benchmarks/revision/consolidated-timings.md) retains component clocks, qualifications and source references. [Original file locations and checksums](../benchmarks/provenance.csv) identify the imported evidence; [consolidation source hashes](../benchmarks/revision/consolidated-sources.json) identify the selected records. Scripts are preserved in [benchmarks](../benchmarks/README.md) with their original execution assumptions. Large datasets and source archives remain outside this small-file collection.

Selected records: [artificial-LD measurements](../benchmarks/results/gsuite/genomic_20k_50k/manuscript-results/20261004/measurements.csv), [reference-derived simulation measurements](../benchmarks/results/gsuite/genomic_20k_50k/manuscript-results/20261004-real-1000g/measurements.csv), [historical gene-set and PoPS records](../benchmarks/results/gsuite/genomic_20k_50k/manuscript-results/20261005-structured/completed-stage-measurements-current.csv), and [correlation timing and memory](../benchmarks/results/website-data/gcorr-current-timings-memory.csv).

Memory is resident working set, not result size, incremental solver allocation or machine RAM. Missing memory stays missing. These evidence tables reuse existing measurements; no new analysis was run to produce this overview.
